title: InMotion Hosting Review 2026: Plans, Prices, Speed Tests and 90-Day Guarantee
excerpt: InMotion gives you 90 days to get your money back and fast shared hosting near the US. Here is what renewal costs, how it tested, and who should skip it.

meta._yoast_wpseo_title: InMotion Hosting Review 2026: Prices, Speed, Guarantee
meta._yoast_wpseo_metadesc: InMotion Hosting review for 2026: shared plan prices and renewals, speed and uptime from independent tests, the 90-day guarantee, pros and cons.
meta.rl_answer: InMotion shared hosting is fast for small sites, with a 90-day money-back guarantee on its own page. Launch renews at 4.0 times its sale price, and WooCommerce checkout was slower in tests.
meta.rl_faqs:
Is InMotion Hosting good? | Yes for small and medium sites. Webhostingcat measured a 100% GTmetrix score, and SimonHosting measured 99.99% uptime.
How much does InMotion cost? | Launch starts at $3.49 a month on the longest term and renews at $13.99. Power is $4.49 renewing at $17.99, and Pro is $8.49 renewing at $24.99.
Does InMotion have a money-back guarantee? | Yes. InMotion's own page lists a 90-day money-back guarantee.
How fast is InMotion? | Webhostingcat measured a 135 ms time to first byte and a 333 ms Largest Contentful Paint on a Los Angeles shared plan.
Is InMotion good for WooCommerce? | For small stores, yes. Webhostingcat saw a 775 ms time to first byte at checkout, and advises a managed host for heavy traffic.
Does InMotion include backups? | TechRadar says backups are not included on shared plans.
Does InMotion include a free domain? | Yes. Reviewers list a free domain for the first year and free SSL on shared plans.
Does InMotion have AI features? | We found no AI builder or assistant. The chat widget on its site is an AI bot.
How steep is the InMotion renewal price? | Launch renews at $13.99 a month, 4.0 times the $3.49 sale price. Pro renews at 2.9 times.
Does InMotion have a Black Friday sale? | Its homepage shows up to 70% off, valid through 1 December 2026, 12 p.m. ET.
Is InMotion better than Hostinger? | InMotion has a longer money-back window. Hostinger has a lower entry price, a lower renewal and more AI tools.
Who should avoid InMotion? | Owners of busy stores, people who want AI tools and anyone who wants the lowest price for years.

meta.rl_takeaways:
Webhostingcat measured 135 ms time to first byte and no errors at 1,000 concurrent clients.
SimonHosting measured 99.99% uptime over 30 days.
InMotion's own page lists a 90-day money-back guarantee.
Launch renews at $13.99 a month, 4.0 times the $3.49 sale price.
meta.rl_r_verdict: InMotion shared hosting is a fast, low-risk way to start a small or medium business site, because you have 90 days to get your money back. Budget for a renewal several times the sale price, and look elsewhere for a busy store.
meta.rl_r_buy:
You run a small or medium business site with light to moderate traffic.
You want a long money-back window.
You want a free domain and unlimited bandwidth.
meta.rl_r_skip:
You expect heavy traffic or run a busy WooCommerce store.
You want built-in AI tools.
You want the lowest price for years.
meta.rl_r_pros:
Fast results near the US in two tests.
No errors at 1,000 concurrent clients in one test.
A 90-day money-back guarantee on shared plans.
Unlimited bandwidth, a free domain and free SSL.
Clear setup guides.
meta.rl_r_cons:
Renewal is 4.0 times the sale price on Launch.
No backups on shared plans, according to TechRadar.
WooCommerce checkout was slower in one test.
meta.rl_r_best: Small and medium business sites with light to moderate traffic
